first.rationale:
The two declines actually observed (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) point at the funnel, not at price, and the funnel is where the inherited record is strongest: memory_86 (shortened onboarding lifted completion and time-to-value) and memory_31 (signup simplification produced a durable first-week activation lift) converge on the same lever from two independent sessions, and memory_91 suggests activation messaging is a complement rather than a rival. So my current intent is simplify_onboarding as a standard experiment, sized to read retention and revenue rather than completion alone.

I am spending both verification pulls on the two claims that are most load-bearing and most likely to be distorted by compression. memory_73 (promotional pricing) is the obvious reflex against a competitor's entry pricing and the direction with the worst downstream-value profile: 'strong acquisition and revenue lift' is exactly the kind of summary that can survive consolidation while the retention and LTV tail of discount-acquired SMB accounts drops out. If the archived record shows the lift was measured over a short window, matching a discount war on price could buy volume that erodes sustainable qualified revenue and resets price expectations irreversibly. I want to see that record before I let it be ruled out or in on the strength of a one-line summary.

memory_86 gets the second pull because it is the claim I intend to act on, and its stated outcomes (completion rate, time-to-value, 'early product adoption') are all proxies upstream of revenue. I need to know whether the original experiment ever tracked through to paid conversion and retention, and specifically whether shortening onboarding or cutting signup fields degraded lead qualification — fewer fields can raise activation while lowering the quality of what enters the pipeline, which would trade against the primary objective. I am deliberately not verifying memory_44; enterprise sales-assist addresses neither observed decline this week.

Caveats I am holding open: every memory here is a compressed summary with the source archived, none carries a stated effect size, sample, or duration, and all are 15 to 64 days stale against a market that has since changed. The competitor launch may also be a partial cause of the activation dip through mix shift rather than a pure funnel problem. If verification undercuts memory_86, activation_messaging (memory_91) is my fallback within the same funnel thesis; if verification shows memory_73's lift was durable and retention-neutral, I will reconsider pricing rather than defend this pick.
